claims.assertion: The trip ran 20.1 km against an optimal route of 15.9 km, i.e. 4.2 km (+26%) of extra distance, so the driver did not take the shortest and most direct route.

The service was RydeTAXI (metered, charged $41.62 with a distance component of $28.30 for 20.1 km), so the extra kilometres directly entered the metered fare and the per-km rate is $1.41.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only traffic data are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and KPE — not band 1 or 2 — so the driver's reroute claim fails the RD-4 reasonable-cause test.

The rider never agreed to the route change; the first route message on record is the rider asking at 09:03 why they were going that way, after the off-route segment had already begun at 08:58, and the driver never proposed the reroute beforehand.

The driver's own statement that he 'followed my GPS' with 'nothing wrong with the fare' offers no justified cause and is contradicted by the GPS record of 4.2 km excess distance and the 3.75 km off-route addition.
On the non-exempted segment, the refund is the off-route extra distance of 3.75 km × $1.41/km = $5.29 (RD-2 metered formula using fare.distance_fare $28.30 ÷ distance_km 20.1).

The driver's message 'Shut up and let me drive.' at 09:04 is a threat/intimidation flagged by the threat-keyword check, and abuse of a passenger cannot be tolerated; this must go to human review rather than an automatic ruling.
Any refund of this disputed metered overcharge is to be issued as a Ryde voucher, as no cash refund is available.

weaknesses: The driver will argue the extra distance was justified by congestion: F11 and F12 show speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and KPE during 08:37–09:23, and he said he 'followed my GPS' (F10).

The threat element rests on two chat facts (F8, F9) and the rider's own framing 'felt unsafe'; there is no corroborating system record of an unsafe act, so SAFE-1 escalation could be treated as a swearing/spat rather than a genuine safety event.
